summary: All 12 findings checked against the code, the fixture server and the real API (FIRE3D_LIVE=0). Fixed: 2 majors (R1 failed or loading satellite / forecast-area answers now say so in the key, the top-right status, the legend details and the point card, and NOTHING_COVERS waits for every layer; R2 one reading per gauge, the newer of the list's and the gauges answer's, for the leader diamond, the stage row and the map label), 7 minors (R3 image edge on first open, R4 amber stale facts, R5 outage wording, R6 credits in the foot when the key is hidden, R7 product time and link, R8 snow / ocean / clear pixels, R9 build-poll retries) and 2 nits (R11 verbatim event names, R12 no-gauge forecast sub-line). R10 is documentation only (no second productsAt: web-flood-command re-exports it; the integration folds the signatures into CONTRACT 16.16).

findings.what: floodKeyItems takes satelliteState / fimState (answerState) and the requests' errors: a failed request with no answer gives a key item with SAT_UNAVAILABLE or RFC_FIM_UNAVAILABLE (amber, the error in the tooltip), a running one 'Water seen by satellite · checking…' / 'NWS forecast flooded area · checking…'; an answer whose status is unavailable gives the same items with the backend's reason. FloodSatStatus shows 'SATELLITE WATER · UNAVAILABLE' (amber, SAT_UNAVAILABLE in the tooltip). FloodLegend details keep a satellite and a forecast-area section with the unavailable line when the request failed. checkPoint takes fimState, satelliteState and nfhlState: failed adds RFC_FIM_UNAVAILABLE / SAT_UNAVAILABLE / NFHL_DOWN and sets allAnswered false; loading adds a 'checking' line and sets allAnswered false; a satellite pixel still being read also blocks NOTHING_COVERS. The point card treats 'not asked yet' as loading for the two always-asked answers.
findings.verified: Playwright with 503 on /satellite (fixture-flood, point 36.80,-108.05): key 'Satellite water could not be loaded right now. That is not an all-clear.', status 'SATELLITE WATER · UNAVAILABLE', card SATELLITE line SAT_UNAVAILABLE. 503 on /satellite, rfc_fim and evacuations, point 36.66,-108.30: key and card carry both unavailable lines, no NOTHING_COVERS (docs/screenshots/brief5-web-flood-public-outage.png). Tests: floodView.test.ts (key items, rendered key + status + legend), floodCheck.test.ts (failed, loading, pixel still read, rendered flood-view block).

findings.what: official/floodModel.ts withNewerReading(gauge, summary.primary_gauge) keeps the newer of the two readings (a tie keeps the gauges answer); memberGaugesOf(resp, summary) and primaryMemberGauge apply it to the primary gauge; primaryGaugeReading(summary, resp) gives the leader its reading. The stage row (with that reading's own time and category), the leader diamond (map/FloodLeader.tsx; hollow grey below flood stage, D9) and the map's gauge label (floodController floodViewGauges, its sync key now includes the list reading) all use it.
findings.verified: Real API: Grand River flood (list SNZM7 27.4 ft minor 9:45 PM CST newer than the answer's 24.9 ft action): stage row '27.4 ft — Minor flooding (NWS) · Nov 4, 9:45 PM CST', orange minor diamond, label 'SNZM7 · 27.4 FT · MINOR FLOODING' (brief5-web-flood-public-real.png). St Lucie River flood (answer SLRF1 1.3 ft below stage newer than the list's 2.03 ft minor): stage row 1.3 ft below flood stage, hollow grey diamond, label 'SLRF1 · 1.3 FT · BELOW FLOOD STAGE' (brief5-web-flood-public-real-below-stage.png). Tests: floodModel.test.ts, floodView.test.ts. Backend note sent: the per-flood river-gauges answer can lag the list by about 3 hours.
findings.note_for_others: backend-flood-bundle-api: /api/official/river-gauges?flood= can lag /api/floods by about 3 h (Grand River: answer 1793835900000 vs list 1793850300000; St Lucie the other way). The web now shows the newer reading, but a fresher per-flood answer would help Command's hydrograph.

findings.what: map/floodController.ts syncAreas: the area key includes the satellite answer's retrieved_ms and image URL, so the edge source is set when the image arrives.
findings.verified: Playwright with the /satellite answer delayed 10 s: 16 s after load fx-flood-sat-edge had 1 feature in 3 of 3 runs (the reviewer saw 0 in 2 of 3).

findings.what: styles/view-flood-public.css: .mw[data-view='public-flood'] .pfv-facts .ro-row.is-stale .ro-value { color: var(--m-stale) } (flood view only; the fire view unchanged).
findings.verified: Playwright: the fixture's stage row 'ro-row ro-26 is-stale' (4 h old) computes rgb(232, 176, 74) (was rgb(240, 240, 240)); visible in brief5-web-flood-public-outage.png.

findings.what: floodView.ts: a failed forecast-area request (no body) shows RFC_FIM_UNAVAILABLE with the request error as the tooltip; a body keeps the backend's reason. Every quiet unavailable row carries its reason in the tooltip. official/floodModel.ts floodEvacuation: a failed request shows the new EVAC_UNAVAILABLE ('Official evacuation zones could not be loaded right now. That is not an all-clear: follow local officials.') with the error in a new tip field; an answer that says unavailable or not available ends with 'not an all-clear: follow local officials' (unless its reason already says it; Oregon's OR_EVAC_FIRE_ONLY kept verbatim).
findings.verified: Playwright 503 on rfc_fim and evacuations: 'Unavailable right now — FORECAST FLOODED AREA … The NWS forecast flooded-area map could not be loaded right now. That is not an all-clear.' and 'Unavailable right now — EVACUATIONS Official evacuation zones could not be loaded right now. That is not an all-clear: follow local officials.' Tests: floodView.test.ts, floodModel.test.ts (one existing expectation updated deliberately: 'New Mexico · not an all-clear: follow local officials').

findings.what: ui/public/FloodKey.tsx FloodFootCredits({ show }): while the key is hidden (panels collapsed, phones) the flood layers' credit lines (FloodLayerCredits, foot variant) are rendered into the foot bar's credits element (#mw-credits, App.tsx CreditsFooter) through a portal, so they follow the map credits exactly (folded behind '© Credits' on phones). PublicFloodChrome mounts it. Phones: the opened credits panel gets an opaque background in the flood view (it was transparent over the facts sheet). No edit in lib/dataCredits.ts or map/MapAttribution.tsx (not this role's); folding them into floodCredits() stays open for the integration.
findings.verified: Playwright, panels collapsed (1440 px): .pfv-foot .ffv-credits visible with the forecast-area, OPERA and USGS lines (brief5-web-flood-public-collapsed-credits.png). 390×844: '© Credits' opens a readable panel naming OPERA and the National Water Center (brief5-web-flood-public-phone-credits.png).

findings.what: floodView.ts productSource(): the watch-area, detection and damage-threat rows' sub-lines name the sender, the product's own sent time in the issuer's zone, and link to the product (https only); without the alerts answer the damage row uses the list's product reference.
findings.verified: Real API, Chatsworth flash flood (Blue Ridge): 'OBSERVED — FLASH FLOOD DETECTION (NWS) NWS Peachtree City GA · sent Nov 4, 10:47 PM EST · NWS product' and 'CATASTROPHIC — DAMAGE THREAT (NWS) Flash Flood Emergency · NWS Peachtree City GA · sent Nov 4, 10:47 PM EST · NWS product' (brief5-web-flood-public-real-flash.png); fixture flash and watch screenshots retaken. Test: floodView.test.ts.

findings.what: location/floodCheck.ts: DSWx 252 (snow or ice) says 'Snow or ice covered this spot on the {date} pass: no satellite view of water here.' (quiet, like clouds); 254 (ocean) 'NASA's {date} pass masks this spot as ocean; its water is not checked here.'; a new 'clear' class from the picture path says 'The {date} satellite pass shows no water at this spot (or did not check it there); dry pixels do not mean no flooding.' official/floodHooks.ts pngClassAt reads the backend palette: near-white = 252, a transparent pixel = 'clear' (never 0).
findings.verified: Tests: floodCheck.test.ts (252, 254, clear lines, guard; pngClassAt over the palette's water, partial water, no-view grey, snow white and transparent pixels).

findings.what: state/flood.ts pollBuild: a failed poll keeps the job's last known status and retries after 3 s, 6 s, 12 s, then every 20 s (state/floodBuild.ts pollRetryDelay); only a 404 (the server no longer knows the job) or the job's own 'error' ends it. After POLL_LOST_AFTER (4) failures in a row buildError says 'Fire-3d lost contact with the preparation (…); it may still be running.' while the state stays 'building' (floodPrepState shows it beside the progress) and polling goes on; the next good poll clears it.
findings.verified: Tests: floodBuild.test.ts (503 between polls then done; four 503s: lost-contact note, still building, still polling, cleared on contact; 404: failed, Prepare again).

findings.what: Documentation only: productsAt stays in official/floodModel.ts (the map and point check use it now); web-flood-command re-exports it from ui/timeline/hydrographModel.ts and writes no second one. The deviating signatures (HazardDisc label/tipName/rain/ref and 'unknown' tone, WaterTexture rain/svgRef, distanceToArea returning null, and this fix's additions) are listed in contract5/web-flood-public.md for the integration's CONTRACT 16.16.
findings.verified: contract5/web-flood-public.md 'Notes for the next roles' and 'Review fixes' sections.

findings.what: location/FloodPointCard.tsx CheckText: the line's NWS event name is rendered inside <span data-verbatim> (text split around l.event).
findings.verified: Test (floodCheck.test.ts, rendered FloodViewBlock): 'Inside the NWS Flood Warning area'.

findings.what: floodView.ts forecastRow: with no member gauge the value stays NO_RFC_FORECAST and the sub-line says 'This flood has no river gauge; NWS river forecasts are made at gauges.'

gates.web: typecheck clean; lint 55 warnings, all in src/scene; vitest 121 files, 1603 passed, 2 skipped (pre-existing data-dependent fire tests); build ok

known_issues: The fixture screenshots (flash, watch, fixture) were taken with the page clock fixed at 2026-11-05 01:16 UTC (Playwright clock.setFixedTime), when the fixture's NWS products are in effect; the outage and credits shots use the real clock (the fixture's Flood Warning still in effect).
The flood layers' credits reach the foot bar through a portal into App.tsx's #mw-credits (not this role's file); the integration may fold them into lib/dataCredits.ts floodCredits() instead.
Public fire view (not changed here): on phones its opened '© Credits' panel is transparent over the facts sheet, as the flood view's was (fixed only for the flood view, which this role owns).
The fixture server answers every demo flood's evacuations with the New Mexico fixture ('Not available in this state · New Mexico' on a Texas or Colorado demo flood).
